newsitem.title: USA: Fingerhut says judge dismisses usury suit.
newsitem.headline: Fingerhut says judge dismisses usury suit.

text.p: Fingerhut Cos Inc said Tuesday it won a favorable decision on March 5 when the Minnesota District Court granted the company's summary judgment and dismissed a suit alleging violation of usury laws.

The marketing company said the suit, Howard et al. v. Fingerhut, was filed in January 1996 and alleged that Fingerhut sales violated usury laws. It said the court found that Fingerhut's credit sales fell within Minnesota's judicially created time price doctrine and were not usurious.
"We vigorously defended the charges and feel completely vindicated by the court's action," Michael Sherman, senior vice president and general counsel, said in a statement.
